The Kano State Government has commenced the development of a 20-year Water Supply and Distribution Master Plan to guide investment and reforms aimed at ensuring sustainable access to potable water across urban and rural communities. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, disclosed this on Friday during a press conference in Kano. He described the initiative as the second time such a long-term blueprint was being undertaken in the state’s history since the administration of the late Governor Audu Bako. “This master plan is part of our broader efforts to address persistent water shortages, improve distribution infrastructure and ensure sustainable access to safe drinking water across the state,” Hashim said. The commissioner said the government had recorded progress in restoring water supply to several communities in metropolitan Kano following the rehabilitation of the Challawa Water Treatment Plant and repairs to sections of the distribution network. Communities benefiting from the restoration include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Kwanar Dala, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Aikawa, Dukurawa, Kabara, Darma, Agadasawa, Kofar Wambai, Dukawa, Mandawari, Daneji, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. Hashim noted that some residents, including those in Alfindiki, had endured between two and three decades without running tap water. He stated that rehabilitation of the water facilities and distribution network was still ongoing, with more than 45 repair and replacement interventions already completed in different locations. “The restoration of water pressure has exposed weaknesses in parts of the old distribution infrastructure, resulting in leakages and pipe bursts that require immediate attention,” Hashim said. The commissioner added that rehabilitation work was continuing at the Tamburawa Water Treatment Plant and other facilities to increase the volume of treated water available for distribution. He also announced the formal establishment of the Kano State Small Towns Water Supply Agency (KASSTOWA), with Engineer Sani Bala Danbatta appointed as Acting Managing Director and Aminu Mamman Yaro as Acting Deputy Managing Director. Hashim urged residents to protect public water infrastructure and warned against unauthorised pipeline connections, vandalism and indiscriminate drilling around major water lines. “Protecting water infrastructure is a shared responsibility. Residents must report burst pipes, leakages and suspected vandalism to the appropriate authorities,” he said. The commissioner said the state government remained committed to improving access to safe and reliable drinking water across Kano. Hussaini Ibrahim
